text: The United States moved to force the sale or ban of TikTok between 2024 and 2025 primarily due to national security concerns regarding potential Chinese government access to US user data and the platform's algorithm, which had been under CFIUS review [Source: ev-1]. On April 24, 2024, President Biden signed the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act, requiring ByteDance to divest its US operations within roughly 270 days, extendable by an additional 90 days, or face a domestic ban [Source: ev-1]. The dispute was resolved through an Oracle-led deal announced on June 10, 2025 [Source: ev-1]. This agreement structured the US operations as a joint venture rather than an outright sale, with Vice President JD Vance leading White House negotiations [Source: ev-1]. Under this arrangement, ByteDance retained a majority interest while Oracle received about a 12.5% stake in TikTok's US operations, joined by SoftBank and other investors [Source: ev-1]. Following the initial enforcement pause via an executive order on January 20, 2025 that delayed action for seventy-five days, the final ownership structure was completed through 2025 with the app remaining live [Source: ev-1].
